notes: Badin was carved out of Hyderabad district in 1975 (Sindh Population Welfare Department says established 1975; Wikipedia says by bifurcation of Hyderabad), so it was not a district at the 1951, 1961 or 1972 censuses but was one at 1981 and 1998.
source_title: Population Welfare Department, Government of Sindh - Badin; Wikipedia - Badin District

notes: Dadu existed in 1951 (1951 census village list for Dadu District exists); it had been created in 1931 from Larkana district talukas (Mehar, Khairpur Nathan Shah, Dadu, Johi, Sehwan) plus Kotri and Kohistan talukas of Karachi district, and lost Jamshoro only in 2004.
source_title: Wikipedia - Dadu District (citing District Government Dadu and Univ. of Sindh Dadu campus pages); NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list no. 30E

notes: Ghotki was split from Sukkur district in 1993 according to the 1998 District Census Reports of both Ghotki (p.10) and Sukkur (p.11) as cited on Wikipedia; the Wikipedia list-of-districts page gives 1983 instead, which conflicts with the census reports and is treated as an error.
source_title: Wikipedia - Ghotki District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Ghotki, PCO, p.10); Wikipedia - Sukkur District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Sukkur, Census publication Vol. 41, PCO 1999, p.11)

notes: Hyderabad was one of the three original British districts of Sindh (1843) and existed at every census; it lost Thar and Parkar (1882), Nawabshah (1912), Badin (1975) and, after 1998, Matiari, Tando Allahyar and Tando Muhammad Khan (2005).
source_title: Wikipedia - Hyderabad District, Sindh (citing Census of India 1921 Vol. 8 for the 1912 split and Dawn 5 Apr 2005 for the 2005 splits)

notes: The district existed in 1951 under the name Upper Sind Frontier District (1951 census village list no. 30E(3) uses that name) and has been called Jacobabad since 1952 according to the 1998 District Census Report of Jacobabad as cited on Wikipedia; it briefly included the Nasirabad subdivision after 1961, and Kashmore was split off only in 2004.
source_title: Wikipedia - Jacobabad District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Jacobabad, Census publication Vol. 17, PCO 1999); NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list no. 30E

former_names: Karachi District; Federal Capital Area/Territory (1948-1961); Karachi Division districts East, West, South (1972), Central and Malir (1996); City District Karachi (2000/2001)
notes: Karachi was a single district (the Federal Capital Area, outside Sind province) at the 1951 census and a single Karachi district within West Pakistan's Karachi(-Bela) Division at the 1961 census; Wikipedia (uncited) says it was split into Karachi East, West and South in 1972 (infobox: August 1972, i.e. just before the September 1972 census, so its 1972 status is unclear), Central and Malir were added in 1996, so at the 1981 and 1998 censuses Karachi was three and five districts respectively, and the single 'Karachi City District' used by the PCO 1951-98 publication was only formally created in 2000/2001 under the devolution plan (restored to five districts 11 July 2011).
source_title: Wikipedia - Karachi Division (1972 split, 1996 Central and Malir, 2001 merger; citing The News International 11 Jul 2011 for restoration); Wikipedia - Administrative divisions of Karachi (1948 FCT, 1961-70 Karachi-Bela Division, 2000 City-District); Wikipedia - Karachi District (Sind) (citing Dawn 23 May 2023 for 1948 FCT)

notes: Khairpur was a princely state enumerated separately alongside Sind at the 1951 census (the 1951 census office was the 'Provincial Superintendent Census, Sind and Khairpur State') and became an ordinary district when the state was amalgamated into West Pakistan in 1955 (Wikipedia infobox: established 15 October 1955; state disestablished 30 September 1955), so its territory is a constant unit across all censuses even though it was not legally a district in February 1951.
source_title: Wikipedia - Khairpur District; Wikipedia - Khairpur (princely state) (citing Daily Times 6 Feb 2018 'Khairpur: then and now'); NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list (Office of the Provincial Superintendent Census, Sind and Khairpur State)

notes: Larkana existed in 1951 (1951 census village list no. 30E(7)); it was formed on 1 August 1901 from talukas of Karachi (Sehwan, Johi, Dadu) and Shikarpur/Sukkur (Mehar, Kakar, Warah, Larkana, Labdarya, Kambar, Ratodero) districts, lost Dadu in 1931 and Qambar Shahdadkot only in 2004/2005.
source_title: Wikipedia - Larkana District (1901 formation uncited on page); NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list no. 30E

notes: Mirpur Khas, which had been the headquarters town of the old Tharparkar district since 1906, became a separate district on 31 October 1990 when Tharparkar district was divided into Mirpur Khas and a reduced Tharparkar (headquarters moved to Mithi), so before 1990 its area is inside the Tharparkar figures; the PCO 1951-98 publication also folds Umerkot (1993-2000) into Mirpur Khas.
source_title: Wikipedia - Mirpur Khas District; Wikipedia - Tharparkar (31 Oct 1990 split, uncited); Wikipedia - Mithi (citing Eco Tourism Development in Pakistan, 'Tharparkar', for 1990 separation)

notes: Naushahro Feroze was a taluka of Nawabshah district until it was given district status on 15 November 1989 (Wikipedia; the 1998 District Census Report of Nawabshah, p.10, as cited on Wikipedia, confirms the 1989 separation), so it is a 1998 unit only.
source_title: Wikipedia - Naushahro Feroze District (date uncited on page); Wikipedia - Shaheed Benazirabad District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Nawabshah, PCO 2000, p.10)

notes: Nawabshah existed in 1951, having been created on 1 November 1912 from the northern talukas of Hyderabad district; it lost Shahdadpur and Sinjhoro talukas to the new Sanghar district in 1953/54 and Naushahro Feroze in 1989, and was renamed Shaheed Benazirabad in 2008.
source_title: Wikipedia - Shaheed Benazirabad District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Nawabshah and Dawn 17 Sep 2008); Wikipedia - Hyderabad District, Sindh (citing Census of India 1921 Vol. 8 for the 1912 split)

notes: Contrary to the working assumption, Sanghar did NOT exist as a district at the February 1951 census: it was created from Shahdadpur and Sinjhoro talukas of Nawabshah and Sanghar and Khipro talukas of the old (pre-1990) Tharparkar district, with the District Disaster Management Authority plan and UN OCHA giving 1954 and several Wikipedia pages giving 1953, and the 1951 census village lists show no Sanghar district.
source_title: Wikipedia - Sanghar (citing Disaster Risk Management Plan District Sanghar, DDMA 2016, and ReliefWeb/OCHA 2014 for 1954); UN OCHA ReliefWeb - Pakistan Emergency Situational Analysis District Sanghar June 2014; Wikipedia - Sanghar District (1954; 1941 taluka note); Wikipedia - Shaheed Benazirabad District (1953, uncited)

notes: Shikarpur was split from Sukkur district in 1977 according to the 1998 District Census Report of Sukkur (p.11) as cited on Wikipedia (Shikarpur page infobox also gives 1977), so it was a district at the 1981 and 1998 censuses only; historically the British Shikarpur district (1843) had been renamed Sukkur in 1901.
source_title: Wikipedia - Sukkur District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Sukkur, Census publication Vol. 41, PCO 1999, p.11); Wikipedia - Shikarpur District

former_names: Shikarpur District (renamed Sukkur District in 1901; headquarters moved to Sukkur 1883)
notes: Sukkur existed in 1951 (1951 census village list no. 30E(4)) as the successor of the British Shikarpur district renamed in 1901; it lost Shikarpur in 1977 and Ghotki in 1993, so its 1951-1981 figures cover those two districts as well.
source_title: Wikipedia - Sukkur District (citing 1998 District Census Report of Sukkur, PCO 1999); NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list no. 30E

former_names: Eastern Sindh Frontier District (1860-1901); Thar and Parkar District (1901-1947); Tharparkar District with headquarters Mirpur Khas (until 1990)
notes: A Tharparkar district existed at every census (1951 census village list no. 30E(6)), but the pre-1990 unit with headquarters at Mirpur Khas covered the 1998 Tharparkar, Mirpur Khas and Umerkot districts (and until 1953/54 the Sanghar and Khipro talukas); on 31 October 1990 it was divided and the name Tharparkar was kept for the desert part headquartered at Mithi.
source_title: Wikipedia - Tharparkar (1882 bifurcation from Hyderabad; 31 Oct 1990 split; 17 Apr 1993 Umerkot); Wikipedia - Mirpur Khas District; NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list no. 30E

notes: Thatta was formed in 1948 from the parts of Karachi district left in Sind when Karachi city became the Federal Capital Territory, and already appears as 'Tatta District' in the 1951 census village lists (no. 30E(2)); it lost Sujawal only in 2013.
source_title: Wikipedia - Sind Province (1936-1955) (citing Dawn 'Karachi & Sindh' 10 Oct 2018); Wikipedia - List of districts in Sindh; NIER library record, Census of Pakistan 1951 Village list no. 30E (Tatta District)

district_1998: UMERKOT DISTRICT (not a 1998 PCO unit; folded into MIRPUR KHAS)
notes: Umerkot WAS a separate district at the March 1998 census: PBS publishes 'Umerkot District at a Glance' with its own 1998 population of 663,095 and 4 talukas (Umerkot, Samaro, Kunri, Pithoro), and the PCO 1951-98 table folds it into Mirpur Khas only because it was abolished and merged into Mirpur Khas on 1 December 2000 (revived by notification dated 13 December 2004); it was constituted in 1993 (Wikipedia Tharparkar page: 17 April 1993 'carved out of Tharparkar', Umerkot pages: from Mirpur Khas, both being parts of the pre-1990 Tharparkar district).
source_title: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics - Umerkot District at a Glance (1998 census); Wikipedia - District Government of Umerkot (1993 constitution, merger 01-12-2000, revival notification 13-12-2004); Wikipedia - Umerkot District (citing ReliefWeb/OCHA 2014); Wikipedia - Tharparkar

district_1998: KARACHI EAST DISTRICT (not a 1998 PCO unit; part of KARACHI CITY DISTRICT)
notes: Karachi East was created in 1972 (Wikipedia infobox: August 1972, uncited) when Karachi district was divided into East, West and South, lost Malir in 1996, existed at the 1981 and 1998 censuses (a separate 'District Census Report of Karachi East 1998' was published by the PCO in 2000), and was merged into City District Karachi in 2000/2001 before being restored on 11 July 2011; its status at the September 1972 census is unclear because the split is dated to the month before.
source_title: Wikipedia - Karachi East District (citing The News Tribe 11 Jul 2011 for restoration); State Bank of Pakistan Library catalogue - District Census Report of Karachi East 1998 (PCO 2000); Wikipedia - Karachi Division

district_1998: KARACHI WEST DISTRICT (not a 1998 PCO unit; part of KARACHI CITY DISTRICT)
notes: Karachi West was created in 1972 as one of the three districts of Karachi Division (Wikipedia, uncited), existed at the 1981 and 1998 censuses (a separate 'District Census Report of Karachi West 1998' was published by the PCO in 2000), was merged into City District Karachi in 2000/2001, restored 11 July 2011 and lost Keamari in 2020.
source_title: Wikipedia - Karachi West District; State Bank of Pakistan Library catalogue - District Census Report of Karachi West 1998 (PCO 2000)

district_1998: KARACHI SOUTH DISTRICT (not a 1998 PCO unit; part of KARACHI CITY DISTRICT)
notes: Karachi South was created in 1972 as one of the three districts of Karachi Division (Wikipedia, uncited), existed at the 1981 and 1998 censuses, was abolished into City District Karachi in 2000/2001 and restored on 11 July 2011.
source_title: Wikipedia - Karachi South District (citing The News Tribe 11 Jul 2011 for restoration); Wikipedia - Karachi Division

district_1998: KARACHI CENTRAL DISTRICT (not a 1998 PCO unit; part of KARACHI CITY DISTRICT)
notes: Karachi Central was created in 1996 as a fourth/fifth district of Karachi Division (Wikipedia; the specific pre-1996 district it was carved from is not found), existed only at the 1998 census, was abolished into City District Karachi in 2000/2001 and restored on 11 July 2011.
source_title: Wikipedia - Karachi Central District; Wikipedia - Karachi Division

district_1998: MALIR DISTRICT (not a 1998 PCO unit; part of KARACHI CITY DISTRICT)
notes: Malir was created in 1996 by bifurcation of Karachi East district (Wikipedia, uncited), existed only at the 1998 census among the five, was abolished into City District Karachi in 2000/2001 and restored on 11 July 2011.
source_title: Wikipedia - Malir District; Wikipedia - Karachi Division
